- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overestimates continuation; reduce forecast slope or add early mean-reversion bias.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent high, model underestimates rally; increase forecast by 1–2% relative to recent peak.
- Model frequently underestimates true outcome in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply slight upward bias to first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment followed by a rebound, model often misses the reversal; add a 2–3 day lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment to forecast.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to underestimate mean reversion; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive over last 7 days.
- If forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, model is underestimating trend; increase forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment shifts.
